input: Source fabric to make reusable produce bags

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The type of fabric (mesh, muslin, cotton, linen, etc.) drastically changes where to source it and how much to buy — mesh needs different suppliers than woven fabric.
A tight budget steers toward bulk discount fabric stores or repurposing existing material; a flexible budget opens up specialty or organic suppliers.
Whether the bags are for personal use, as gifts, or to sell determines the quantity needed and the quality bar required.
The number of bags planned drives how many yards of fabric to source and whether buying by the yard or in bulk makes more sense.
Priorities like washability, organic certification, transparency (so checkout scanners can read barcodes), or weight affect which fabric types qualify.
Whether the user wants to shop locally (fabric stores, thrift shops) or online changes the search strategy and lead time entirely.
Knowing what 'good enough' looks like — lowest cost, certified organic, minimal packaging, fastest delivery — sets the priority when trade-offs arise.

gold.taskTitle: Source fabric for reusable produce bags
gold.taskDescription: Find and obtain suitable fabric to sew reusable produce bags for carrying or storing fresh produce.

questions.title: What fabric type are you aiming to use?
questions.description: Identify the preferred fabric — e.g., fine mesh, muslin, cotton voile, linen, or recycled material — as this determines which suppliers are relevant.

questions.title: How many bags are you planning to make?
questions.description: Establish the target quantity of bags to calculate yardage needed and decide between buying by the yard vs. bulk rolls.

questions.title: Who are the bags being made for?
questions.description: Determine whether the bags are for personal use, gifts, or resale, as this affects the quality standard and total volume required.

questions.title: What is your budget for the fabric?
questions.description: Establish a spending limit to filter sourcing options between budget discount retailers, mid-range fabric stores, and premium or organic suppliers.

questions.title: Do you prefer shopping locally or ordering online?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred sourcing channel — local fabric or craft stores vs. online retailers — to tailor the search accordingly.

questions.title: Are there specific material properties the fabric must have?
questions.description: Identify non-negotiable qualities such as organic certification, see-through mesh for barcode scanning, machine-washability, or a maximum weight per bag.

questions.title: What does a successful fabric purchase look like to you?
questions.description: Define the top priority when trade-offs arise — lowest price, fastest delivery, eco credentials, or a specific feel and durability standard.
